questions.q: Which URL follows common REST naming for fetching one account's transactions?
o: `GET /accounts/42/transactions`
`GET /getTransactionsForAccount?id=42`
`POST /accounts/42/fetchTransactions`
`GET /account/transactionList/42`
questions.w: Use plural nouns for resources and let the HTTP method express the action. Avoid verbs in paths.

questions.q: Which HTTP methods are idempotent by definition?
o: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE`
`POST` and `PATCH`
`POST` and `DELETE`
`GET` and `POST`
questions.w: Repeating them leaves the server in the same state. `POST` usually creates a new resource each time, so protect it with an idempotency key.

questions.q: A client creates a payment successfully. Which response is the best fit?
o: `201 Created` with a `Location` header for the new resource
`200 OK` with an empty response body
`204 No Content` with a `Location` header
`202 Accepted` with the final balance in the body
questions.w: `201` signals a new resource. Use `202 Accepted` when processing continues asynchronously.

questions.q: A request body is well-formed JSON but breaks a business rule, such as an overdraft. Which status is the best fit?
o: `422 Unprocessable Entity` (or `400`) with a clear error body
`500 Internal Server Error` with a stack trace
`404 Not Found` because the rule failed
`401 Unauthorized` because the request is invalid
questions.w: `4xx` means the client can fix the request. `5xx` means the server failed. Return a consistent error body, for example RFC 7807 problem details.

questions.q: How do you prevent two clients from overwriting each other's updates to the same resource?
o: An `ETag` with `If-Match` for optimistic concurrency
Always use `POST` for every update
Lock the resource for an hour per client
Return `200` for every update request
questions.w: The server returns `412 Precondition Failed` when the version no longer matches, and the client re-reads before retrying.

questions.q: Why prefer cursor-based pagination over offset for large, changing data sets?
o: Results stay stable under inserts and deep pages stay fast
Clients can jump straight to page 500
Every row is returned in a single response
Sorting is no longer needed on the query
questions.w: `OFFSET 100000` scans and discards rows, and inserts shift pages so items repeat or vanish. A cursor continues after the last seen key.

questions.q: What is a safe way to change an API without breaking existing clients?
o: Add optional fields and endpoints, and version before breaking changes
Rename fields in place and tell clients to update
Remove old fields in the next deployment
Change status codes without telling anyone
questions.w: Clients should ignore unknown fields (tolerant reader). Breaking changes go in a new version such as `/v2` or a header.

questions.q: What does a `429 Too Many Requests` response with `Retry-After` tell the client?
o: The rate limit was exceeded, so wait before sending more
The server is permanently down for good
The URL in the request is wrong
The request body is too large
questions.w: Rate limiting protects the service. Well-behaved clients back off and honour `Retry-After`.
